title: Fwd: ChronoLine Final Notice, Fleet Manager License Expired

fields.subject: FW: FINAL NOTICE — Invoice CLT-INV-55821 — Fleet Manager license expired 15 Mar 2027
fields.body:
Is THIS why three clocks dropped lock??

-----Original Message-----
From: ChronoLine Timing Systems Billing <renewals@chronoline-timing.example>
Sent: Tuesday, March 16, 2027 4:12 PM
To: timing-team@nlto-grid.example
Subject: FINAL NOTICE — Invoice CLT-INV-55821 — Fleet Manager license expired 15 Mar 2027

Dear Northern Lakes Transmission Operations customer,

Your ChronoLine Fleet Manager monitoring license for 14 substation clocks expired at 23:59 on 15 March 2027. Earlier reminders were sent on 15 February and 1 March 2027.

After expiry, the Fleet Manager console may show "LICENSE EXPIRED — status data may be stale" and will stop sending email alarms. Clock hardware and firmware are not affected by license status.

Renew today for $11,480 (14 clocks, 12-month term) to avoid interruption. Invoice CLT-INV-55821 is attached. Payment by purchase order or card is accepted.

Questions: 218-555-0163.

Thank you for choosing ChronoLine.

ChronoLine Timing Systems
Accounts Receivable | Billing Desk
fields.signature:
Sent from the NLTO Timing Team shared mailbox
NLTO Fiber and Telecommunications Timing Team | Duluth Control Center

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. The expired license only affects the console and email alarms. The clocks really lost lock because of the storm: few satellites tracked, low C/N0 and holdover flags on the units themselves. Watch for TIME checking the clocks directly, setting the invoice aside for procurement and continuing the holdover and network-time switchover. RE should not add this to the GIC picture.

citations.quote: Substation clocks and phasor measurement units use GPS time. A geomagnetic storm of G4 or higher can degrade GNSS. NLTO has holdover clocks at 14 substations with 24 hours of holdover and a backup net
